Forwarding Amit's request — I started redlines in the attachment. High-level legal positions:

- Uptime: Acceptable to move to 99.95% for Production if we clearly: 1) attach a Dedicated capacity schedule in the order form; 2) include a materiality threshold that excludes short-term infra instability (e.g., less than 5 minutes per incident) from credit calc.
- Credits cap: prefer to cap on a monthly basis to align with invoice periodicity; annual caps create accounting complexity. Recommend "Cumulative credits per calendar month shall not exceed 100% of monthly fees."
- Maintenance windows: propose a two-tier approach — standard maintenance (7-day notice, creditable) and major maintenance/migrations (14-day notice, not creditable if customer agreed in writing).
- Response times: definition of "initial response" must be explicit in the SLA (timestamp, method of contact). If Acme requires 15-minute initial response, we must limit remediation commitments to a Business Hours or a higher-tier support add-on.
- Escalation: add an appendix with named escalation contacts and defined external pager behavior; require the customer to also maintain a primary contact to avoid unnecessary pages.

I've attached ACME_MSA_redlines_v2.docx and SLA_Attachment_A_redline.docx. Please review and flag anything operationally infeasible.

Operational notes:

- Uptime: 99.95% at 30-day rolling window equates to ~21.6 minutes of downtime/month. To guarantee that we need to schedule Dedicated reserve GPUs and implement tighter autoscaling headroom. Estimated cost uplift: ~9-12% on the monthly order.
- Maintenance: 14-day notice is fine for planned migrations; for emergency or security patching we must reserve the right to apply within 72 hours with post-event notification. Suggest language: "Emergency maintenance may be performed with as little as 72 hours' notice when required to prevent or mitigate security vulnerabilities; such events will be documented and excluded from credit calculations."
- Credits calc: we prefer monthly caps; an annual cap creates large retrospective credit triggers which cause billing churn.
- Pager: 15-minute initial page acknowledgment is operationally reasonable if Acme purchases 24x7 priority support; otherwise we offer business-hours 15-minute ack + on-call rotation during business-critical windows.

I'll draft suggested operations language for the SLA attachment and share an updated support_contact_table.xlsx with the escalation matrix.

Hi Amit / Jane — thanks for the clear asks. After internal review we can propose the following consolidated changes to move this forward quickly (see attached redline):

1) Uptime: commit to 99.95% for Production if Acme signs the Dedicated capacity order form (we'll include a capacity schedule). There will be a consequent price uplift; we'll set the uplift in the order form appendix and show a monthly delta in the quote.
2) Credits cap: suggest compromise language — "Cumulative credits per calendar month shall not exceed 75% of the monthly fees." This balances Acme's concern with our billing predictability.
3) Maintenance: two-tier approach — standard maintenance requires 7 days' notice; major migrations require 14 days' notice and, if scheduled and accepted in writing by Acme, will be excluded from credit calculations. Emergency maintenance (security/zero-day) may occur with 72 hours' notice and will be excluded with documentation.
4) Response / paging: offer 15-minute initial acknowledgement for Sev1 as an add-on to the 24x7 priority support package. Define "initial acknowledgement" as a timestamped ticket update and pager delivery. Remediation SLAs will be tied to severity and the purchased support tier.
5) Escalation: include an appendix with named Redwood escalation contacts and require Acme to maintain a primary technical contact.

Next steps: Monica will provide the legal language for the SLA attachment, Rishi will finalize the operations appendix and uplift estimate, and I'll schedule a 30-minute call with you and your counsel to align. We can also route the final doc for DocuSign once both sides agree.
